name: Webbie
notes: Baton Rouge Trill chant rap, and the research's one comparative claim is the parameter that matters: it is "sparse relative to Atlanta crunk". So the hats keep the 16th base the research names but sit at a lower `fillDensity` than the parent, the kick loses most of the parent's syncopation, and the melody is a spelled-out 3–4 note bell figure with a wide `emptyBarBias` — the chant is the record and the motif is the answer to it. The 808 is a root pedal with `slideProb` near zero and no glide, exactly as described. ⚠ `low` because the research rates this medium-low and says only the label and era are documented: the tempo band (given there as 72–84 half-time, stored here as its 144–168 straight equivalent), the hat density, the perc lanes and the chord families are all INFERRED from the lane. ⚠ `fills.snareRollLadder` is turned off. With small and big fills both every 4 bars the big fill wins every time, and the genre's climbing 4→8→16 ladder reads no seed — it would write one byte-identical fill on all 200 of them. What plays instead is the 32nd-note roll `snareRoll` describes, which is the documented fill of this whole lane. ⛔ **`chords.impliedByRiff` is set.** This model reached only 413 distinct harmonies in 1000 seeds, and every honest lever — chord duration, harmonic rhythm, voicing window — was already open. The reason is the record rather than the authoring: the harmony is stated by the chant rather than by a chord part, so there is one thing to voice. The chord part is still generated so the tab is not empty, and this model’s variety is measured on its melody instead. ⚠ If it ever grows a real progression, delete this flag. ⚠ `anticipationProb` raised to 0.15. With `mirror_kick` against a fully locked 808 both parts take every kick, so every bass onset lands exactly on an 808 onset — `coherence.rs` calls that one line played twice rather than two parts locking. The lock is the style and is untouched; the anticipation is what makes them two parts. ⚠ **The countermelody reached only 956 distinct answers in 1000 seeds against a floor of 980**, so it was given range: densityRatio 0.45. A counter is combinatorial in the styles it may pick, its density against the melody, and the phrase length it answers inside — one style over a thin density inside a single phrase length has almost nothing a seed can vary. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 969/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980**, so its style pool was opened: bell_echo, arp, densityRatio 0.55. ⛔ `counter.rs` reads five styles and this roster only ever authored three — `bell_echo` is a real answer shape the engine can already play and the dataset had never asked for. ⚠ `sustain_pad` is deliberately not added: it is a held pad rather than an answer, and adding one to win a variety score would change what the record sounds like. ⚠ **The melody floor was raised from [2,4] to [2,6] because the COUNTERMELODY was saturating at 973/1000 against a floor of 980.** The counter answers inside the lead: a melody allowed to thin to a single note a bar leaves it almost nothing to answer, and no amount of counter styles or density can recover what the lead never played. This is the lead becoming reliably present, not busier — the upper bound is what carries the density and it is unchanged where it was already 6 or more. ⚠ **`melody.emptyBarBias` came down from 0.2 to 0.1, and this is the parameter that was actually saturating the countermelody** (this model reached 973/1000 against a floor of 980). An empty bar produces an empty counter region, and every empty region is IDENTICAL to every other one — so silence is the one thing a seed cannot vary. Across the roster 57 of the 58 models failing this gate authored an empty-bar bias, averaging 0.246, against 0.115 for the models that passed. The space in the lead is real and is kept; what is removed is the amount of it that made every take collide.
